title: Embedding Model Fine-Tuning
summary: Adapt the retrieval representation to domain relevance using trustworthy examples, hard negatives, and a controlled re-indexing migration.
overview: Embedding fine-tuning changes how queries and documents are represented so distances better reflect a target domain’s relevance judgments. Training can use positive query-passage pairs, graded similarity, triplets, or other objectives suited to the available data. The goal is retrieval quality, not simply lower training loss or closer vectors for superficially similar text.

Good negatives are central: passages that look similar but do not answer the query teach useful distinctions. False negatives can teach the opposite, especially when several passages are valid answers. A new embedding model changes the geometry of the index, so corpus vectors and query vectors must migrate together rather than mix incompatible spaces.

production.poc: A prototype compares a strong general embedding baseline with a small domain adaptation on held-out queries.
production.production: Production separates training and evaluation by source or time, audits negatives, and measures retrieval recall under real filters.
production.scale: Enterprise scale versions datasets and models, builds parallel indexes, evaluates tenant and language slices, and plans rollback without recomputing everything during an incident.

components.name: Relevance dataset
components.role: Stores query-passage judgments with provenance and leakage controls.

components.name: Negative miner
components.role: Finds confusing nonrelevant passages for expert or rule-based validation.

components.name: Training pipeline
components.role: Applies an objective compatible with the dataset format and base model.

components.name: Retrieval evaluator
components.role: Measures held-out recall and ranking across representative slices.

components.name: Index migration controller
components.role: Re-embeds the corpus and switches query routing between compatible versions.

flow.title: Diagnose baseline errors
flow.description: Confirm that representation quality, rather than parsing or filtering, causes the retrieval gap.

flow.title: Build clean examples
flow.description: Collect supported positives and validate negatives, including alternative correct answers.

flow.title: Train and version
flow.description: Record base model, tokenizer, objective, dataset revision, and configuration.

flow.title: Evaluate independently
flow.description: Test unseen queries and sources, including general-domain regression cases.

flow.title: Build a new index
flow.description: Encode corpus documents with the adapted model and validate dimensions and normalization.

flow.title: Roll out gradually
flow.description: Route a controlled cohort to the new query encoder and matching index, then compare task outcomes.

useCase.title: Distinguishing similar process defects
useCase.situation: An engineering assistant searches defect-analysis reports containing closely related process terminology.
useCase.problem: General embeddings rank visually similar but causally unrelated defect reports above the useful analysis.
useCase.requirement: Improve retrieval of relevant process conditions without memorizing report text.
useCase.architecture: Experts label query-report pairs and validate hard negatives from the existing retriever.
runtime: The adapted encoder is evaluated on unseen lots and later reports.
A parallel index supports a controlled comparison with the unchanged baseline.
useCase.failure: If one process family improves while another regresses, routing remains on the baseline until the data or objective is corrected.
useCase.impact: Track recall by defect family, false-negative labeling rate, and downstream evidence support; training loss alone cannot justify migration.

tradeoffs.cost: Needs trustworthy labels and ongoing evaluation.
May introduce false negatives without validation.
Temporarily doubles embedding and storage work.

failures.detection: Near-duplicate reports appear in training and test sets.
failures.recovery: Split by source lineage, time, or business entity.

failures.detection: Distances become unreliable despite successful queries.
failures.recovery: Enforce encoder-index compatibility at routing time.

mistakes.fix: Repair source and chunk quality first.

mistakes.mistake: Treating every unclicked result as negative
mistakes.fix: Validate relevance and account for alternative answers.
Migrate query and corpus representations together.

whenToUse: Use when domain vocabulary causes measured retrieval errors.
Use with enough reliable relevance examples.
Use when gains justify corpus re-embedding.
whenNotToUse: Avoid training on noisy unreviewed feedback alone.
Do not adapt when filters or missing documents cause the problem.
Avoid deployment without a held-out baseline comparison.
